Speaker's Card/Request to Speak: If you would like to address the City Council on a scheduled agenda item, including a Consent Calendar item, a Regular Council Business item, a Public Hearing item, or Public Comments, please complete the "Request to Speak Form." The card is at the table at the entrance to the City Council Chamber. Please identify on the card your name and the item on which you would like to speak and return to the City Clerk. The "Request to Speak Form" assists the Mayor in ensuring that all persons wishing to address the City Council are recognized. It also ensures the accurate identification of meeting participants in the City Council minutes. Your name will be called at the time the matter is heard by the City Council. City policy is to limit public testimony to up to three minutes per speaker depending on relevant circumstances (unless the time limit is extended by the Mayor), which includes the presentation of electronic or audio visual information. Speakers may not yield their time to other persons.
Please take notice that the order of scheduled agenda items below and/or the time they are actually heard, considered and decided may be modified by the Mayor or the City Council during the course of the meeting, so please stay alert.

NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC
LIVE BROADCASTING AND REBROADCASTING
Regular City Council meetings are broadcast live every 2nd and 4th Tuesday of the month at 4 p.m. and are replayed on Tuesdays at 4 p.m. (in weeks in which there is not a live City Council meeting), Sundays at 11 a.m., Wednesdays at 7 p.m., and Thursdays at 10 a.m. until the next City Council meeting. All broadcasts can be viewed on Cox Communications Local Access Channel 30 and U-Verse Channel 99. City Council meetings are also available via live webcast and at any time for replaying through the City's ICTV webpage at cityofirvine.org/ictv . For more information, please contact the City Clerk''s office at (949) 724-6205.
ADJOURNMENT
At 11:00 p.m., the City Council will determine which of the remaining agenda items can be considered and acted upon prior to 12:00 midnight and will continue all other items on which additional time is required until a future City Council meeting. All meetings are scheduled to terminate at 12:00 midnight.
STAFF REPORTS
As a general rule, staff reports or other written documentation have been prepared or organized with respect to each item of business listed on the agenda. Copies of these materials are on file with the City Clerk and are available for public inspection and copying once the agenda is publicly posted, (at least 72 hours prior to a regular City Council meeting). Staff reports can also be downloaded from the City's website at cityofirvine.org beginning the Friday prior to the scheduled City Council meeting on Tuesday.
In addition, meetings can be viewed live at the time posted on the agenda and related staff reports can be opened and viewed simultaneously along with the streaming of the meeting. To view the meeting, go to cityofirvine.org/ictv .
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk staff at (949)724-6205.
SUPPLEMENTAL MATERIAL RECEIVED AFTER THE POSTING OF THE AGENDA
Any supplemental writings or documents distributed to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after the posting of the agenda will be available for public review in the City Clerk''s Office, One Civic Center Plaza, Irvine, California, during normal business hours. In addition, such writings or documents will be made available for public review at the respective public meeting.
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk staff at (949)724-6205.
SUBMITTAL OF INFORMATION BY MEMBERS OF THE PUBLIC FOR DISSEMINATION OR PRESENTATION AT PUBLIC MEETINGS
Media Types and Guidelines
1. Written Materials/Handouts:
Any member of the public who desires to submit documentation in hard copy form may do so prior to the meeting or at the time he/she addresses the City Council. Please provide 15 copies of the information to be submitted and file with the City Clerk at the time of arrival to the meeting. This information will be disseminated to the City Council at the time testimony is given.
2. Large Displays/Maps/Renderings:
Any member of the public who desires to display freestanding large displays or renderings in conjunction with their public testimony is asked to notify the City Clerk's Office at (949)724-6205 no later than 12:00 noon on the day of the scheduled meeting so that an easel can be made available, if necessary.
3. Electronic Documents/Audio-Visuals:
Any member of the public who desires to display information electronically in conjunction with their public testimony is asked to submit the information to the Public Information Office (PIO) no later than 12:00 noon on the day of the scheduled meeting. To facilitate your request contact the PIO Office at (949)724-6253 or the City Clerk''s Office at (949)724-6205.
Information must be provided on CD, DVD, or VHS; or, emailed by 12:00 noon on the day of the scheduled meeting to pio@ci.irvine.ca.us . Members of the public will be asked to provide their name, identify the meeting and the agenda item to be addressed, and a day time phone number.
The PIO office will notify the person submitting the information as soon as possible prior to the meeting if the information cannot be accessed or if the version provided is incompatible with the City''s system. Every effort will be made by City staff to facilitate the presentation.
CITY SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS
It is the intention of the City of Irvine to comply with the Americans With Disabilities Act (ADA) in all respects. If, as an attendee or a participant at this meeting, you will need special assistance beyond what is normally provided, the City of Irvine will attempt to accommodate you in every reasonable manner. Please contact the City Clerk's Office at (949)724-6205.
Assisted listening devices are available at the meeting for individuals with hearing impairments. Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting. (28 CFR 35. 102-35. 104 ADA Title II)
CHALLENGING CITY DECISIONS
The time limit within which to commence any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City is governed by Section 1094.6 of the Code of Civil Procedure, unless a shorter limitations period is specified by any other provision. Under Section 1094.6, any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City must be filed no later than the 90th day following the date on which such decision becomes final. Any lawsuit or legal challenge that is not filed within this 90-day period will be barred.
If a person wishes to challenge the nature of the above actions in court, they may be limited to raising only those issues they or someone else raised at the meeting described in this notice, or in written correspondence delivered to the City of Irvine, at or prior to the meeting. In addition, judicial challenge may be limited or barred where the interested party has not sought and exhausted all available administrative remedies.
COMMUNICATION AND ELECTRONIC DEVICES
To minimize distractions, please be sure all personal communication and electronic devices are turned off or on silent mode.
MEETING SCHEDULE
Regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesdays of each month at 4:00 p.m. Study Sessions and/or Closed Sessions are periodically held prior to the start of the regular meeting. Agendas are available at the following locations:
 City Clerk's Office
 Police Department
 Front Entrance of City Hall
 University Park Center (Culver/Michelson)
 Walnut Village Center (Culver/Walnut)
 Northwood Town Center (Irvine Blvd./Yale)
 City's web page at www.ci.irvine.ca.us

MINUTES

  CITY COUNCIL
  REGULAR MEETING

  February 28, 2017
  City Council Chamber
  One Civic Center Plaza
  Irvine, CA 92606

CALL TO ORDER

The regular meeting of the Irvine City Council was called to order at 4:13 p.m. on
February 28, 2017 in the City Council Chamber, Irvine Civic Center, One Civic Center
Plaza, Irvine, California; Mayor Wagner presiding.

ROLL CALL

  Present:  4  Councilmember:  Melissa Fox
  Councilmember:  Jeffrey Lalloway
  Councilmember:  Christina Shea
  Mayor:  Donald P. Wagner

  Absent:  1  Mayor Pro Tempore:  Lynn Schott

1.  SCOPING SESSION

  1.1  GENERAL PLAN AMENDMENT FOR A RESIDENTIAL UNIT AND NON-
  RESIDENTIAL BUILDING INTENSITY REALLOCATION WITHIN
  PLANNING AREA 12 (OAK CREEK) AND PLANNING AREA 40
  (CYPRESS VILLAGE)

  Tim Gehrich, Deputy Director of Community Development, presented the
  staff report and responded to questions. Stephanie Frady, Senior Planner,
  was also available for questions.
 City Council Minutes  February 28, 2017

  The following individuals spoke in opposition to the proposed projects due
  to high density and/or increased traffic:

  Rebecca Ward, Irvine resident
  Alan Meyerson, Irvine resident
  Carl Mariz, Irvine resident

  City Council discussion included: potential traffic impacts on Jeffrey and
  Sand Canyon; whether existing traffic circulation on Sand Canyon at
  California Interstate 5 (I-5) could be mitigated in the near future;
  questioned trip generation during peak times; noted the need for
  alternative transportation; noted the potential impact on schools; noted
  gaps in funding for affordable housing, and working collaboratively with
  the Irvine Company and the Irvine Community Land Trust to fulfill the
  different housing needs; noted citywide transportation as a top priority and
  suggested review of the projects by the Transportation Commission;
  expressed concern about surrounding noise levels from I-5 and the nearby
  railroad tracks; noted that the projects would be further analyzed during
  the application review process; inquired about project intensity and the trip
  conversion process between residential and non-residential zoning; and
  questioned the tentative timeline for Commission and City Council review.

  Michael Leblanc, representing the Irvine Company, provided a brief
  overview of the projects, summarized the benefits to the City, and
  reiterated the company’s commitment to work collaboratively.

  ACTION:  Moved  by  Councilmember  Shea,  seconded  by
  Councilmember Fox, to:

  Defer the proposed General Plan Amendment pending review by the
  Transportation Commission and a comprehensive review of the
  General Plan by the City Council.

  ACTION:  A substitute motion was made by Councilmember Lalloway,
  seconded by Mayor Wagner, to:

  Receive and file.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  2
 City Council Minutes  February 28, 2017

  The motion failed as follows:

  AYES:  2  COUNCILMEMBERS:  Lalloway and Wagner

  NOES:  2  COUNCILMEMBERS:  Fox and Shea

  ABSENT: 1  COUNCILMEMBERS:  Schott

  Following discussion, Councilmember Shea amended her motion.

  ACTION:  Moved  by  Councilmember  Shea,  seconded  by
  Councilmember Fox, to:

  Defer the proposed General Plan Amendment pending review by the
  Transportation Commission and a comprehensive review of the
  General Plan by the City Council, and return to the City Council
  within six months.

  The motion failed as follows:

  AYES:  2  COUNCILMEMBERS:  Fox and Shea

  NOES:  2  COUNCILMEMBERS:  Lalloway and Wagner

  ABSENT: 1  COUNCILMEMBERS:  Schott

  ACTION:  Moved by Councilmember Lalloway, seconded by Mayor
  Wagner, to:

  Process the application.

  The motion failed as follows:

  AYES:  2  COUNCILMEMBERS:  Lalloway and Wagner

  NOES:  2  COUNCILMEMBERS:  Fox and Shea

  ABSENT: 1  COUNCILMEMBERS:  Schott

  At the request of Councilmember Lalloway, City Manager Joyce was
  directed to return with the item at the next City Council meeting.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  3
 City Council Minutes  February 28, 2017

  2.  CLOSED SESSION

  City Attorney Melching announced the following Closed Session item:

  2.1  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL - EXISTING LITIGATION -
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(1) - one case: Irvine
  Community News & Views et al. v. City of Irvine (USDC Case No. 8:16-
  cv-00208-AG(JCGx))

  There were no requests to speak to the Closed Session item.

  RECESS

  Mayor Wagner convened the City Council meeting to Closed Session at 5:32 p.m.

  RECONVENE TO THE CITY COUNCIL MEETING

  Mayor Wagner reconvened the regular City Council meeting at 6:25 p.m. City Attorney
  Melching, on behalf of the City Council, announced that there was no reportable action
  taken in Closed Session.

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Mayor Wagner led the Pledge of Allegiance.

  INVOCATION

  Mayor Wagner invited Pastor Benn Prescott from Free Chapel OC in Irvine to provide
  the invocation.

  CITY MANAGER'S REPORT

  There was no report.

  ANNOUNCEMENTS/COMMITTEE REPORTS/COUNCIL REPORTS

  Councilmember Fox made the following announcements:

  •  On Friday, February 24, Irvine teenager Teresa Johnston was critically
  injured by a falling tree during one of the recent storms, and noted that a
  YouCaring site was established by the family to help with their daughter’s
  extraordinary medical costs. For information, visit YouCaring.com and type
  her first and last name, or visit the “Irvine Gives” webpage on the City’s
  website at cityofirvine.org.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  4
 City Council Minutes  February 28, 2017

  •  The Trust for Public Land released its 2016 Park Score Index for the 100
  largest U.S. Cities, ranking Irvine first in Southern California, second in the
  State of California, and eighth nationwide.

  •  Based on the recent incident at the Jewish Community Center, a community
  forum will be held in the near future to assure residents, as well as those
  who traverse the City for work or school, that the City Council was
  committed to public safety. Councilmember Fox also requested that the City
  Manager agendize the matter at the next City Council meeting.

  Mayor Wagner made the following announcements:

  •  The community is invited to a dedication ceremony for a new community
  center at Quail Hill Community Park on Saturday, March 4. During the
  event, the center will be open for self-guided tours from 4-6 p.m, and will
  begin regular operating hours after the event. The event is free, no RSVP
  needed.
  •  The City, in partnership with Orange County United Way, Irvine Valley
  College, and the Orange County One-Stop Center, is offering free tax-
  preparation services to taxpayers who live, work, or attend school in Irvine
  and earned less than $60,000 in 2016. Qualifying taxpayers can receive
  help filing their taxes from IRS-trained and certified volunteers, who will also
  assist them in receiving the Earned Income Tax Credit when applicable. For
  information, including a list of locations for free tax-preparation services,
  visit cityofirvine.org or unitedwayoc.org.

  •  On Monday, February 27, the Merage Jewish Community Center in Irvine
  received a threat by telephone, one of as many as 21 threats reported
  against Jewish facilities around the nation. The Irvine Police Department
  responded to facilitate the safe evacuation of everyone on site, and no
  injuries were reported. Mayor Wagner reiterated that the City Council
  continues to stand unambiguously with Jewish friends and residents in
  condemnation of this and any other hate crimes, and provided assurance
  that the Irvine Police Department was thoroughly investigating the crime.

  ADDITIONS AND DELETIONS

  There were no additions or deletions to the agenda. However, City Manager Joyce
  noted that Item 5.6 (Contract Award for Maintenance of Landscape and Athletic
  Facilities at the Orange County Great Park) had been considered by the City Council in
  its capacity as the Orange County Great Park Board earlier in the day; and at the desire
  of the City Council, the record would reflect the discussion and action taken at the
  Board meeting. He also referenced an errata memo with respect to Item No. 3.6.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  5

  Councilmember Fox, who noted concerns within the boundaries of the
  proposed tract maps, and questioned the ability of the City Council to
  address such concerns at this stage of the approval process.

  Jeffrey Melching, City Attorney, noted that while a local ordinance allowed
  the City Engineer to approve tract maps, the California Subdivision Map
  Act (Act) required that final maps be presented to the City Council; and
  further noted that although the item was presented into a public meeting
  context as required by the Act, the item was merely a reporting item and
  did not allow the City Council to make any substantive or discretionary
  changes.

  5.1  FORMATION OF CITY OF IRVINE TRANSPORTATION COMMISSION
  AND ADOPTION OF ENABLING DOCUMENTS

  Sean Joyce, City Manager, provided a brief summary of the action was
  taken by the City Council at its January 10, 2017 meeting and presented
  the staff report. He also noted an errata memo dated February 28
  clarifying the proposed powers and duties of the Transportation
  Commission.

  Carl Mariz, Irvine resident, spoke in support, and suggested 1) public
  transportation be a high priority; 2) working collaboratively with the school
  districts to increase bus service; and 3) consideration of light rail and other
  forms of transportation options.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  10
 City Council Minutes  February 28, 2017

  Courtney Santos, Irvine resident, spoke in support of creating
  transportation subcommittees, and suggested that Transportation
  Commission meetings be televised.

  City Council discussion included: creating subcommittees specific to
  active transportation, public transportation, and finance; questioned the
  composition of subcommittees and requirements for those who would
  serve; expressed concern about the potential financial and staff time for
  subcommittees comprised of outside membership; questioned Brown Act
  compliance if subcommittees were comprised of outside members; noted
  upcoming results of the General Plan Amendment outreach; providing the
  Transportation Commission the latitude to create its own subcommittees;
  further clarification of the roles and responsibilities between the
  Transportation Commission and City Council related to transportation
  matters; questioned the process for agendizing transportation matters at
  the request of a Councilmember; and reviewed the scope of the
  Transportation Commission.

  Jeffrey Melching, City Attorney, noted that the creation of subcommittees
  by the Transportation Commission was permissible under the proposed
  bylaws; however, ad hoc committees could only consist of members of the
  committee, which were subject to the Brown Act. He further noted that
  subcommittees consisting of at-large members may be subject to Brown
  Act compliance.

  ACTION:  Moved by Councilmember Shea, seconded by
